headline: World food prices rise 2.5% in August amid Middle East tensions and adverse weather
summary: The FAO Food Price Index rose 1.9% in August from July and 2.5% from a year earlier. The increase reflects adverse weather and supply problems linked to the Middle East crisis.
why: The FAO index tracks global food commodity prices, which influence inflation, central bank policy and agricultural equities worldwide.
